cards.text: Jesus calls the Twelve to Him. These are His twelve disciples, and now He's got a job for them. He's about to send them out.

cards.question: Jesus sends the Twelve out one at a time, each man on his own.
As Jesus sends the Twelve out, He gives them authority. Authority over what?

cards.text: Then Jesus gives them the packing list, and friend, it is SHORT. Shorter than mine when I left the junk drawer, and all I owned back there was dust!

cards.question: Jesus tells the Twelve to take nothing for the journey except one thing. What is it?
Jesus tells the Twelve to pack some bread and keep money in their belts, just in case.
For the trip, Jesus tells the Twelve to wear ___ but not a second ___.

cards.text: Next up, where to sleep. No booking app. No five-star reviews. Jesus has one simple rule.

cards.question: When the Twelve enter a house, what does Jesus tell them to do?

answers.text: Stay there until they leave that area
Move to a new house every night
Pay the owner before they sleep there

cards.text: But Jesus is honest with them. Not every place is going to roll out the welcome mat.

cards.question: If a place won't welcome the Twelve or listen to them, what does Jesus tell them to do as they leave?

answers.text: Shake the dust off their feet

cards.question: Jesus says shaking off that dust is a testimony against the people who wouldn't welcome or listen to the Twelve.

cards.text: Shake the DUST off?! Friend, I spent YEARS wearing dust like a second apron, and NOBODY told me I could just shake it off!
So the Twelve set out, just like Jesus told them. And they start preaching.

cards.question: The Twelve preach that the people should ___.

cards.text: And friend, preaching is NOT all these guys do. Not even close.

cards.question: Besides preaching, what else do the Twelve do as they go?

answers.text: Drive out demons and heal the sick

cards.question: As the Twelve heal many of the sick, they anoint them with ___.

findings.problem: The joke's comparison doesn't work. Papa Dorin says Jesus's packing list is shorter than his own when he left the junk drawer, where all he owned was dust. That means his own list was nothing. Jesus's list still has a staff, sandals and a tunic, so it can't be shorter than nothing. A baker would stop and say "huh?"

rule.text: If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.

findings.problem: This story card has four sentences: "Next up, where to sleep." "No booking app." "No five-star reviews." "Jesus has one simple rule." Only the opening card can be longer than two sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This card is only a joke about verse 11, which cards 10 to 12 already covered. It tells no new part of the passage. The joke should ride along on a card that moves the passage forward, like card 10 or card 14.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: Nothing before this card helps the baker choose between oil, water and myrrh. Card 16 only says preaching isn't all the Twelve do. The right answer is a detail the baker can only guess, just like the Psalm 23 bad example ("What does He anoint David's head with?" with oil, myrrh or perfume). Myrrh is also close enough to oil that a baker could argue for it (Esther 2:12 mentions "oil of myrrh").

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.
